name: Jean-Paul Sartre
role: French philosopher, playwright and public intellectual (1905–1980)
summary: Sartre moved from existentialist individualism to a Marxist-influenced left, backing anti-colonial revolt and criticizing both Soviet interventions and the French Communist Party. In his last years he sided with Maoist and anarchist-leaning movements and defended revolutionary violence by the colonized.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Argued colonial rule dehumanizes the colonized and creates 'slaves and monsters'; it must end, not reform the colonized.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Treated class struggle as a motor of history in his Marxist period, though in 1975 he spoke of two struggles in conversation.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: In Colonialism is a System he condemned the colonial trade, where the colony sells raw materials cheaply and buys French manufactures dear, as viable only if natives work for next to nothing, and demanded an end to colonialism.

death-penalty.rationale: Words point both ways: 'I am so totally opposed to capital punishment' and 'opposed to the death penalty', yet crimes against humanity 'certainly deserve the death penalty' and Algerian rebel generals should be condemned to death then reprieved.

direct-action.rationale: Described the Gauche Proletarienne as seeking power by revolution rather than the ballot, which he said elects only rotten politicians; not stated as a general rule.

dominated-front.rationale: Preface to Fanon calls for Third World unity: revolutionary socialism everywhere together or defeat one by one by the former tyrants.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: If the colonized bourgeoisie takes power, 'the new state, despite formal sovereignty, remains in the hands of the imperialists'; independence is 'an empty word' without agrarian reform and nationalization.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Condemned the Soviet intervention in Hungary ('detest this slaughter') and called the 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia by the Five a war crime.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Treated choosing a Jewish nation with its own soil as a legitimate authentic choice; later favored two independent, equal and free states in Israel-Palestine.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Cited Marx's mode of production of material life as the framework of history in Search for a Method.

national-self-determination.rationale: Acknowledged a people's right to self-determination and supported Breton and Languedoc national struggles alongside anti-colonial ones.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: In the Beauvoir interview said men try to imprison women in a subordinate position and called the women's struggle primary.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Defended the right to strike and criticized regulation meant to channel and limit it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Backed the Russell Tribunal and trial of leaders responsible for crimes in Vietnam; prefaced Alleg's account of torture in Algeria.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the bourgeois single party whose organs are police, administration and army, and whose function is to crush the resistance of the poor.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Argued a left programme needs priority investments, a great proportion public, against American capital.

strong-leader.rationale: Wrote in 1958 that the best way of completing France's ruin would be to entrust it to one 'strong man' who would impose his rules on everybody.

universal-morality.rationale: 'Though the content of ethics is variable, a certain form of it is universal'; to will freedom is to will the freedom of others.

vanguard-party.rationale: Wrote that the working class exists as a class through the Party, though he criticized the Communist Party after 1968.

notes: Themes searched: political violence, revolution, colonialism and neocolonialism, imperial intervention, strikes, the state and party, women, Israel, death penalty, Vietnam, history and ethics. Many statements (taxes, healthcare, immigration, courts, speech, etc.) have no recorded position and stay null. In the 1970s he spoke of an increasingly anarchist outlook, but no statement was found that settles state-harmful.
